transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Jared Wilson (Tidegate Infra PM), Priya Rao (Tidegate Sec), Anika Singh (Platform Eng), Diego Morales (SRE)

Quick summary (auto):
Tidegate is evaluating Redwood for private/VPC deployment. Primary concerns: region gating (EU-only), private endpoints vs peering (cost/latency tradeoffs), egress restrictions, audit logs/KMS, and IP/CIDR planning for transit gateway. Customer asked about dedicated vs hosted for compliance and predictable throughput. Redwood AE/SE committed to network checklist, security docs, and a sample benchmark.

Topics: private endpoints, VPC peering, Transit Gateway, egress/egress IP, KMS/HSM, SOC2, SAML, region lockdown, latency vs cost, DNS and TLS for private endpoints.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: All right thanks everyone for joining, um, we'll kick off — I'm Maya from Redwood, that's Liam our SE. Could we do quick intros?
[00:10] Jared: Jared here, infra, we own the transit gateway and peering stuff.
[00:14] Priya: Priya, security, I'll focus on compliance and KMS questions.
[00:18] Anika: Anika, platform, I'll be doing the integration work.
[00:21] Diego: Diego, SRE, mostly on runbook/egress.
[00:25] Liam: Nice to meet you all. Quick agenda — listen to your constraints, walk through how Redwood handles private deployments, and then dig into specific network/topology questions.

[02:05] Jared: Our big blocker is region gating. We have a hard requirement to keep EU customers' data within eu-west-1 and not exit region. How do you support region-restricted private endpoints?
[02:20] Maya: Sure, good question. Redwood Private offers region pinning for model serving — you can pin requests to a region and we'll deploy inference nodes there. For the VPC side, we provide private endpoints or VPC peering patterns depending on your preference. For strict residency you can run the control plane in a private VPC as well — is that the level of isolation you mean?
[02:40] Priya: Yes, must be EU-only both control plane and data plane, and logs need to be archived in our EU logging account. Also need KMS in our region.
[02:49] Liam: That's supported — Private deployments can be configured with customer-managed KMS and we can route audit logs to your S3 in-region. There's a short sec doc we'll share. Note: for hosted offering we have limitations around region lock but Dedicated or Private on-prem gives full control.

[04:12] Anika: On the network pattern, we're evaluating two options: VPC peering to Redwood managed VPCs, or PrivateLink/Private Endpoint into Redwood. Curious tradeoffs — latency, cost, IP planning.
[04:30] Liam: Right, high-level: VPC peering is a simpler L3 route — generally cheaper for steady egress but you need non-overlapping CIDRs and more IP planning. PrivateLink (or private endpoints) preserves your control plane egress via ENIs and gives you an endpoint per service which can be easier for IP overlap and security but tends to incur per-endpoint pricing, and depending on cloud, slightly higher p99 latency.
[05:05] Diego: Do you have numbers for p50/p95 on both? We care about token latency for short chat requests — sub 120ms ideally for p95 if possible.
[05:15] Liam: Depends on model & sequence length. For smaller TTS-ish models we often see p95 ~80–120ms on dedicated GPU pools when deployed in-region. But with PrivateLink you'll add a small extra RTT, maybe 10–30ms variance depending on cross-AZ path. We'll put timestamped raw numbers in the benchmark doc.

[06:33] Jared: Our transit gateway is NATed through our egress firewall; we have strict egress IP ranges whitelisted by partners. How do we ensure stable egress IPs from Redwood reach partners?
[06:46] Maya: For Dedicated you can have static egress IP ranges allocated to your pool. For hosted we use shared egress IPs which can change. If you need stable egress for partner-whitelisting, Dedicated or Private with egress NAT in your VPC is the typical path.
[07:10] Priya: Also we need mutual TLS and mTLS for service-to-service traffic to the endpoint. Is that available?
[07:18] Liam: We support mTLS termination on PrivateLink endpoints and can require client certs from your side. For peering, we expect TLS on the application layer — you can terminate at your ALB and we accept TLS from there. There are some nuances with ALPN and HTTP/2; we'll document the recommended TLS config.

[09:02] Anika: One constraint — our CIDR ranges are fairly conservative, we have /20s across prod/dev and some overlap with partners. Peering might be a pain.
[09:12] Liam: Yeah that's where PrivateLink shines because it uses an ENI and you address it via endpoint private IPs in your subnet; less risk of CIDR overlap. Downsides: more endpoints to manage and, again, pricing.

[10:45] Diego: What about DNS? We don't want splits or leaks. If we do PrivateLink, does Redwood give you a private zone we can forward to?
[10:55] Liam: We can provide a recommended internal DNS setup and we can publish a Private Hosted Zone link you can conditional-forward. There's also a connector we ship in the Private helm chart that will make SRV records for model endpoints. Small note: sometimes transcriptions say 'kay-vee cache' but that is KV cache — not relevant to DNS.

[12:30] Priya: On the compliance side: SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001, and we'd like proof of encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (CMK). Also need detailed audit logs at token/route granularity.
[12:44] Maya: Understood. For Private deployments, CMK is supported; logs can be exported to your S3/GCS in-region and we can provide field-level audit logs. For Hosted, audit resolution is coarser. We'll include the security questionnaire and SOC2 report.

[14:08] Anika: Are there any limits to model size or KV cache when running in a private VPC? We might want multi-GPU pinned instances for larger models.
[14:18] Liam: The runtime supports shard/replica placements; we can provision dedicated pools with desired GPU types. KV cache size depends on model and cache policy — we can tune cache eviction. For very large models we recommend Dedicated reserved pools so you get predictable ML perf.

[16:35] Jared: Another practical thing — our compliance team requires that control-plane APIs not cross the region. Is it possible to host the control plane (e.g., rollout, model registry) in the same EU tenant?
[16:45] Maya: Yes, Redwood Private offers an option to deploy the control plane in your VPC — that keeps the control plane in-region; otherwise our hosted control plane may be out-of-region for global customers. We'll highlight that in the sec doc.

[18:20] Anika: For peering vs private endpoints, what's the troubleshooting story? Example: how do we trace a request from our app to the model and get per-token latencies?
[18:33] Liam: Our console provides per-request traces and token-level timing for requests routed through Redwood's runtime. In Private you can ship that telemetry to your observability backend, or use our console with data retained only in-region. We'll also provide tracing hooks for distributed traces.

[20:00] Diego: Bandwidth — if we have heavy embedding workloads, will peering saturate our TGW? Should we plan a separate attach?
[20:12] Liam: Heavy throughput workloads usually benefit from reserving Dedicated capacity and isolating traffic, yes. If your TGW is already highly utilized, consider a separate attachment or cross-account peering to Redwood's VPC for the inference traffic, or let Redwood's Dedicated attach to your TGW — engineering can scope that.

[22:50] Priya: One more security nuance — we have a requirement for customer audit to have immutable logs and retention of 7 years. Can Redwood support long-term WORM style retention?
[23:05] Maya: We can deliver logs to your S3 bucket with lifecycle and retention policies you manage. For WORM, we can support it through your own buckets with compliance mode enabled. We'll include the exact flow in the security appendix.

[25:40] Jared: Network MTU and fragmentation — we operate VMs for some workloads and have strict MTU settings. Any gotchas with large request/response payloads?
[25:53] Liam: We generally recommend standard MTU 1500; large streaming payloads may need chunking. Our SDK uses streaming chunks for long outputs to avoid MTU fragmentation. We'll test with your payloads in the benchmark run.

[27:30] Anika: One operational ask: in case of failover we want clear automatic fallback to a cheaper/broader model in another region without sending user PII out-of-region. Can Redwood enforce data residency on fallback?
[27:47] Liam: Good callout. We have routing policies that can prefer in-region variants and will not fall back to an out-of-region model unless explicitly allowed. We can configure failover policies per route, e.g., 'no cross-region fallback'. That is configurable in rollouts.

[29:50] Maya: Quick note on pricing and committed Dedicated — if you commit to a Dedicated pool we can give static capacity and static egress IPs; otherwise hosted is pay-as-you-go but with less IP guarantees.
[30:10] Anika: For procurement, we have to justify cost of Dedicated vs hosted. Is there a simple calculation you provide to compare per-token cost including egress?
[30:22] Maya: We'll provide an example TCO calc — we'll include a worked example in the follow-up spreadsheet based on your expected qps and sequence lengths.

[32:00] Diego: Are there known partner integrations we should be aware of, e.g. with our observability stack?
[32:09] Liam: We have exporters for Datadog, New Relic, and a generic Prometheus scraper for telemetry. Also can push logs to your in-region S3 or GCS.

[34:18] Priya: For identity, we require SAML SSO for the console and RBAC for team roles. Can you integrate with our IdP?
[34:26] Maya: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. For Private deployments SCIM/SSO can be routed to your internal IdP. We'll send the SAML metadata sample.

[36:05] Anika: Any special networking for on-prem bridging? We have one datacenter that will talk to cloud via Direct Connect with a BGP session.
[36:14] Liam: We can support on-prem via Direct Connect or VPN — typical pattern is to either extend your VPC to Redwood via TGW attach or set up a private link and have a BGP session from your DC to the cloud VPC. We'll need your ASN and BGP prefixes to design.

[38:40] Jared: Does Redwood support route-based filters on what models can be called from which subnets or tags?
[38:48] Liam: Yes you can set per-route policies and ACLs that map to subnets or API keys; we support token-scoped restrictions so you can restrict model families per environment.

[40:55] Diego: What's the typical time to onboard a Private deployment? We have a Q4 target for a pilot.
[41:02] Maya: If it's a fairly standard VPC peering or PrivateLink, onboarding can be a couple of weeks including security review. For a full Private control plane in your VPC it can be 4–8 weeks depending on procurement and network approvals. For a Q4 pilot you can start with a Hosted/Dedicated pilot in-region while we run the Private provisioning in parallel.

[43:10] Priya: Regarding encryption in transit: do you support client key pinning or enforced TLS versions?
[43:18] Liam: Yes we can enforce TLS1.2+ and optionally TLS1.3 only; client cert pinning via mTLS is supported for PrivateLink.

[45:30] Anika: For the benchmark, we'll provide a sample corpus of 10k short chats and some batch embedding workloads. Would you run it in eu-west-1 under both peering and privatelink to compare?
[45:42] Liam: Yep, we'll run tests in both patterns and return p50/p95/p99 latencies and token costs. We'll also attach the raw logs to the shared drive.

[47:55] Maya: Ok perf plan — we'll need a test key and a small runbook from you with expected QPS and sequences. I'll follow up via email.

[50:12] Priya: A question on auditability: can we get per-API-key usage and the raw request bodies for debugging, or is that sensitive?
[50:25] Liam: We can store request metadata and obfuscated bodies for debugging; storing full PII in logs is something you control. For Private we can route raw request logs to your secure bucket, but you'll want to consider retention/PII policies.

[52:40] Jared: Let's talk fallbacks — if eu-west-1 capacity is saturated, do you auto-fail to another region or queue? We need deterministic behavior.
[52:50] Maya: Default is to avoid cross-region failover unless you opt in. We can set a policy to queue or return 429s instead. For enterprise Dedicated we can enable burst capacity or autoscale policies. We'll put options in the follow-up doc.

[55:00] Anika: Last logistics — please send the network checklist, sample Terraform snippets for PrivateLink and peering, and the security questionnaire.
[55:10] Maya: Will do. Links: network checklist: https://redwood.example.com/network-checklist, security questionnaire: https://redwood.example.com/sec-questionnaire, terraform samples: https://redwood.example.com/terraform/private-onramp-samples

[56:30] Maya: Recap and next steps — Liam will run the benchmark, I'll send pricing and the docs, Tidegate to share CIDRs and TGW diagram, Priya to confirm compliance items. We'll reconvene after the benchmark. Thanks all.

End of transcript.
